root_cause_class: RC2 / WP2.3 user-private Agora servant visibility on persona GET subroutes
implementation: services/control-plane/bff/personas/service.py: _ensure_persona_exists gains keyword-only viewer_user_id (lazy resolver) and require_exists. Without a viewer it is the unchanged existence check used by write routes. With a viewer it returns when _persona_fleet_record_visible_to(record, None) is true (record not user_private: no scope resolution), otherwise resolves the viewer and applies _persona_fleet_record_visible_to again; a rejected record raises the same 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND ('Persona not found' / 'Persona {id} does not exist') as a missing persona. No second visibility rule.

personas/routes/detail.py: _lazy_viewer_user_id(identity, utc_now, tenant_id=None) wraps the existing _fleet_viewer_user_id (tenant and scope resolve only for a private record). The 9 GET routes pass it to _ensure_persona_exists in the same position as before (after _require_read_role).

personas/routes/lifecycle.py: GET strategy-pool/publish-history passes the viewer after _pool_owner_authorization (original order); the pool-publish service principal keeps the existence-only call because it reads its own publication record and is not a viewer. GET strategy-matches passes the viewer through _persona_strategy_matches_response -> _persona_strategy_discovery_payload (single directory read); POST strategy-discovery passes none and is unchanged.

trade_journal.py: read_owner calls the default _ensure_persona_readable (or an injected ensure_persona_readable) after require_read_role, _allowed and the bound_tenant guard and before any telemetry/persona owner call; it uses require_exists=False so a persona absent from a healthy directory keeps the owner's answer. When the record is absent and the persona registry read is unavailable (PersonaFleetPort source 'unavailable', via the read store's dataset_source('personas'), or a status read that raises), visibility is unknown and the route fails closed with 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE before all four journal owner reads. A genuinely absent persona with a healthy registry keeps the owner answer; a present record is judged as in the persona routes.

personas/service.py: the read variant of _ensure_persona_exists runs in one request_read_scope, so the directory snapshot's two list_personas reads and the registry-status read share one cached persona-registry owner call.
BFF_API_CONTRACT.md states the owner rule for the 15 routes.

write_routes_unchanged.evidence: POST /bff/personas/{id}/strategy-pool/publish and POST .../test-prompt in personas/routes/lifecycle.py still call _ensure_persona_exists without a viewer; POST strategy-discovery reaches _ensure_persona_exists with viewer_user_id=None; the service-principal publish-history path passes no viewer. Asserted in test_read_check_reuses_shared_visibility_rule_and_write_routes_keep_existence_check.
write_routes_unchanged.trade_journal_commands: command() and its _allowed / require_operator_role checks are not touched.

acceptance_evidence.AC1: tests/test_persona_subroute_private_visibility.py::test_non_owner_gets_missing_persona_404_and_no_owner_call and test_owner_still_answered are parametrized over all 15 routes; test_non_owner_404_is_identical_to_missing_persona_on_persona_routes compares the non-owner body with a genuinely missing persona on the 11 persona-router routes. The trade-journal episode route answers the owner with the telemetry owner's own 404 (the stub reports no episode) and the non-owner with the persona 404.
acceptance_evidence.AC2: Visibility is _persona_fleet_record_visible_to + _fleet_viewer_user_id through the one shared check inside _ensure_persona_exists(viewer_user_id=...); routes only pass a lazy viewer. Write routes unchanged (see write_routes_unchanged).
acceptance_evidence.AC3: test_unscoped_and_trading_personas_unchanged_without_scope_resolution (15 routes x {trading persona, servant without owner_scope/visibility_scope}) answers as before with 0 scope resolutions; test_trade_journal_missing_persona_keeps_owner_answer keeps the owner answer for a persona absent from the directory.
acceptance_evidence.AC4: For every rejected non-owner request the counters for memory, audit, telemetry, persona-owner, pool history, route policy, activity, evaluations, capability snapshot, runtime profile and strategy discovery stay 0 (asserted per route).
acceptance_evidence.AC5: BFF_API_CONTRACT.md: new bullet next to the GET /bff/personas owner-visibility bullet.
acceptance_evidence.AC8: Owner Claude2 (Anthropic) and reviewer Codex2 (OpenAI) are different model families.

runtime_budget.new_owner_reads_per_request: Measured with a counted PersonaRegistry transport behind the real PersonaFleetPort (tests/test_persona_subroute_private_visibility.py, journal_harness): every checked request costs exactly 1 persona-registry directory owner call (GET /api/personas on the hosted PersonaRegistryHttpWritePort). _get_persona_directory_snapshot calls list_personas twice, but under the read variant's request_read_scope both hit the same cached pcr_personas key (previously 2 transport calls per unscoped check). Persona-router routes keep their one directory read (now at most 1 transport call). The 4 trade-journal routes gain that 1 registry call before the telemetry/persona owner call; no memory, audit, telemetry or persona-owner call is added, and a rejected or fail-closed request makes none (asserted).
runtime_budget.cadence: Request-scoped in-memory predicate; no new job, timer or emitter.
runtime_budget.size_and_count_at_hosted_scale: No new response fields, files, tables, queues or caches; hides responses for ~5 other-user servants on hosted dev.
